quote: Whenever dharma declines and the purpose of life is forgotten, I manifest myself on earth. I am born in every age to protect the good, to destroy evil, and to reestablish dharma.
You have the right to work, but for the work's sake only. You have no right to the fruits of work.
Perform every action with your heart fixed on the Supreme Lord. Renounce attachment to the fruits. Be even-tempered in success and failure.
You are what you believe in. You become that which you believe you can become.
When meditation is mastered, the mind is unwavering like the flame of a lamp in a windless place.
Death is as sure for that which is born, as birth is for that which is dead. Therefore grieve not for what is inevitable.
The soul can never be cut to pieces by any weapon, nor burned by fire, nor moistened by water, nor withered by the wind.
Perform action, O Arjuna, being steadfast in Yoga, abandoning attachment and balanced in success and failure. Evenness of mind is called Yoga.
The mind is difficult to control and restless; but by practice and by dispassion it may be restrained.
A person can rise through the efforts of his own mind; or draw himself down in the same manner. Because each person is his own friend or enemy.
One who sees inaction in action, and action in inaction, is intelligent among men.
The key to equanimity: act without attachment, treat success and failure alike.
Set thy heart upon thy work, but never on its reward.
Happiness from the senses seems like nectar initially, but it is bitter as poison in the end.
There is neither this world nor the world beyond nor happiness for the one who doubts.
The truly wise mourn neither for the living nor for the dead.
Whenever and wherever there is a decline in virtue and a rise of irreligion, O Arjuna, at that dawn, I appear.
To protect the innocent, to annihilate the wicked, to reestablish righteousness, I birth Myself in every age.
As the ignorant perform their duties with attachment, the learned may act without attachment, to guide.
He who is content with whatever comes, without attachment, not disappointed when he gets nothing, is wise.
Calmness, gentleness, silence, self-restraint, and purity: these are the disciplines of the mind.
For one who has conquered his mind, a mind is best of friends; for one who has failed to do so, it is the greatest enemy.
One who is not disturbed in mind even amidst the threefold miseries or elated when there is happiness, and who is free from attachment, fear and anger, is called a sage of steady mind.
Let your aim be the welfare of all. Then act with devotion and without selfishness.
Even if you are the most sinful of all sinners, yet you shall cross over all sin by the raft of knowledge.
Actions do not cling to Me because I am not attached to their results.
Better is one’s own duty though lacking in merit than the duty of another perfectly performed.
Man is made by his belief. As he believes, so he becomes.
The ignorant work for their own profit; the wise work for the welfare of the world.
The soul is eternal, indestructible; weapons cannot pierce it, fire cannot burn it, water cannot wet it.
Like changing clothes, the soul passes from one body to another.
The soul is never born, nor does it ever die.
They are both ignorant who think the soul kills or is killed.
As the embodied soul continuously passes from boyhood to youth to old age, so at death, it takes another body.
For one who has conquered the mind, the mind is a friend; the uncontrolled mind is one’s greatest enemy.
Perform your prescribed duty, for action is better than inaction.
One who does nothing for sense gratification but works for self-purification merges into self.
The disciplined mind is steady in meditation, like a lamp in a windless place.
He who has no attachments can truly love others, for his love is pure.
There is nothing as purifying as knowledge.
When meditation is mastered, Self reveals itself.
From attachment arises desire, from desire arises anger.
Through meditation, the yogi obtains the peace that resides in the Self.
Even in a land of misery, one who knows it stays free from despair.
Whatever happened, happened for good. Whatever is happening, is happening for good.
Every individual is working out his own salvation.
By selfless service, you will always find fulfillment.
Man is made by his belief. As he believes, so he is.
Let a man lift himself by his own self, and let him not lower himself.
The wise see knowledge and action as one; they see truly.
Reshape yourself through the power of your will.
The self-controlled soul attains peace, abandoning all desires and longings.
The yogi is greater than the ascetic, greater than the empiricist, and greater than the fruitive worker.
Fix your mind on Me alone, let your intellect dwell in Me.
The mind acts like an enemy for those who cannot control it.
Pleasures that arise from contact with the senses are wombs of misery.
Detachment is freedom from desire and sorrow.

He who hates no creature, who is friendly and compassionate to all, free from possessiveness and ego, equal in pleasure and pain, forgiving, contented, steady in meditation, self-controlled, and resolute — he is dear to Me.
Even a little practice of this yoga will save you from great fear.
No effort on the path of self-realization is ever wasted.
Self-realization is the highest knowledge.
Renounce the fruits of action; this brings peace.
Perform your duties without attachment and surrender the results to God.
He who sees Me in all beings and all beings in Me never loses sight of Me.
That which pervades the entire body is indestructible.
The wise grieve neither for the living nor for the dead.
Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer or give, whatever austerities you perform — do that as an offering to Me.
The yogi who is content with whatever comes by chance, who rises above dualities, free from envy, balanced in success and failure, is not bound by actions.
The man of meditation is superior to the man of austerities.
To those who are constantly devoted and worship Me with love, I give the understanding by which they can come to Me.
He who abandons all desires and acts free from longing and ego attains peace.
There is no purifier equal to knowledge.
Those who are motivated only by desire for the fruits of action are miserable.
When a person responds to the joys and sorrows of others as if they were his own, he has attained the highest state of union.
Be steadfast in yoga, O Arjuna. Perform your duty and abandon all attachment to success or failure.
With selfless action, one attains the Supreme.
The wise act without attachment, for the welfare of the world.
By devotion one knows Me truly.
The disciplined person, enjoying sense objects with senses free from attachment and aversion, attains peace.
The person who is not disturbed by happiness and distress is fit for liberation.
Surrender all activities to Me, with your mind focused on the Self.
The yogi who is devoted to meditation on the Self is superior to those engaged in austerity or knowledge.
This Self cannot be cut, burned, wetted, or withered.
Knowing the Self, one transcends all sorrow.
The man of wisdom, united in mind and soul, renounces the fruits of action.
A person is made by faith; as he believes, so he becomes.
The offering given with devotion is dear to Me.
Abandoning all dharmas, surrender unto Me alone.
Those who worship Me with devotion are in Me, and I am in them.
A yogi is greater than the ascetic, greater than the wise, and greater than the man of action.
When the soul achieves peace, it neither rejoices nor hates.
The wise look with equal vision on a Brahmin, a cow, an elephant, a dog, and an outcaste.
Equanimity is called yoga.
Those who worship the demigods go to the demigods; those who worship Me come to Me.
One who offers Me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or water, I accept.
Fix your mind on Me, be devoted to Me, worship Me, bow down to Me.
Renunciation is difficult to attain without yoga.
The person free from attachment, with a steady mind, attains peace.
The ignorant, the faithless, and the doubting perish.
Those who worship Me with unwavering devotion are very dear to Me.
Wherever there is Krishna, the master of yoga, and Arjuna, the supreme archer, there also will surely be glory, victory, prosperity, and sound morality.
